name: Italian fascism
summary: Italian fascism, the movement and regime of Mussolini, holds that the nation is an ethical and spiritual whole created by and inseparable from the State, to which individuals, classes and private interests are subordinate. It rejects liberal democracy, Marxian socialism and pacifism in favour of rule by a single party and leader, class collaboration through state-supervised syndicates and corporations, war and expansion as signs of national vitality, a revived Roman heritage, and from 1938 a biological racism.
scope: The movement and regime of 1919-1943 as set out in Mussolini's 'Doctrine of Fascism' (1932), Alfredo Rocco's 1925 address endorsed by Mussolini, Gentile's 'Philosophic Basis of Fascism', Mussolini's speeches, the labour laws of 1926-34, the 1929 Lateran Treaty and the 1938 Manifesto of Race. The radical 1919 programme counts only where it stayed in force. Nazi biological racism as a system, later neo-fascist movements and the Salo Republic are excluded.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Doctrine repudiates pacifism and exalts war.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Doctrine (section 6) spurns teleological conceptions of a final systematisation of the human race, the premise of eventually abolishing money.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: The Doctrine rejects Marxian socialism and prizes labour inside the Corporative System; Rocco keeps private enterprise and rejects collective organisation of production.

alienated-labor.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the Marxist critique of capitalist exploitation in favour of class collaboration.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Rocco keeps individual property rights as part of Fascist doctrine and rejects the socialist abolition of private property.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Doctrine repudiates pacifism and holds that war alone brings all human energies to their highest tension.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The Doctrine treats war as human nature and national vitality, not as a product of capitalism.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The Doctrine rejects popular consultation and deliberation by lot.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Doctrine (section 8) says the Corporative System 'conciliates every interest in the unity of the State', and Rocco replaces strikes and lockouts by justice among the classes through the State.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Doctrine denies that class war is the driving force of history.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Doctrine (section 9) says 'the worship of church power' is a thing of the past and makes the State the highest authority.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Mussolini's 1919 speeches demand frontiers at the Brenner and the Adriatic, with the annexation of Fiume and Dalmatia, citing the martyrs who held that Italians live there.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the vote and rule by numbers, so communal voting rolls are foreign to it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The Doctrine holds that struggle between peoples drives vitality and history.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The Doctrine (section 8) allows 'no individuals nor groups' outside the State, so local bodies bound to carry out assembly decisions are rejected.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the myth of happiness and says action should be moved by holiness and heroism instead of economic motive.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Recognised employer and worker associations concluded collective agreements binding on the whole occupational category, and the National Council of Corporations fixed wage and salary rates.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Doctrine makes the state the source of all value, so state building comes first.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Doctrine presents fascism as the opposite of Marxian socialism and rejects class war and materialism, so coexistence is not sought.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The Doctrine glorifies war and national loyalty and rejects pacifism, so working for one's own government's defeat is treason.

democracy-becomes-oligarchy.rationale: The Doctrine (section 6) says democratic regimes give the people 'the illusion of being sovereign' while real sovereignty rests in other, often secret, forces.

democracy-best.rationale: The Doctrine (sections 6 and 7) denies that numbers can govern by periodical consultations and rejects the 'absurd conventional falsehood of political equality'.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Doctrine rejects rule by numbers through periodic consultation as the test of government.

democratic-peace.rationale: The Doctrine rejects democracy and pacifism and holds war as ennobling, so spreading democracy for peace is rejected.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Doctrine denies class struggle as history's engine and rejects Marxian socialism, so class dictatorship is refused in favour of a national state above classes.

direct-votes.rationale: The Doctrine (section 6) denies that numbers can govern 'by means of periodical consultations'.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The Manifesto of Race says the European character of Italians 'must not be altered in any way' and that crossing with any extra-European race alters it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The Doctrine affirms inequality and opposes the materialist socialism behind this idea.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Doctrine (sections 10 and 12) makes the State the creator of right and denies it its own theology; authority comes from the State, not from God.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Doctrine (section 2) places the individual 'within the orbit of duty' to the nation, with sacrifice of particular interests even by death.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The Doctrine (section 3) says all international creations are 'extraneous to the spirit of Fascism', accepted only for passing utility.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Doctrine places no limit on the state, which is absolute; entrenched rights against it are rejected.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Britannica records that the regime passed several antisemitic laws in 1938, singling out Jews for discriminatory treatment, which contradicts equal rights before the law.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The Doctrine praises the immutable, beneficial and fruitful inequality of mankind, so adherents reject levelling of outcomes.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The Doctrine allows no groups outside the State and puts economic life under its Corporative System.

harm-principle.rationale: The state limits liberty by its own aims; individual liberty is a margin it grants.

independent-unions.rationale: Associations were bodies governed by public law, one recognised per category, grouped under State-supervised confederations, and the corporations were organs of the State.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Doctrine holds that individuals exist only within the state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Doctrine (section 12) says 'the State has no theology, but it has morality' and (section 9) rejects 'worship of church power'.

leader-cult.rationale: Gentile says the Party and propaganda exist to make the Duce's thought and will the masses' own.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism (section 11) holds that the crisis of capital 'cannot be resolved except by the State and in the State' and mocks the liberal demand that industry be left in peace, and it opposes liberalism 'both in the political and in the economical field' (section 8).

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Doctrine (section 13) says Fascism 'has had its Fallen and its martyrs' as proof it is a faith.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Doctrine explicitly rejects the materialist conception of history and the notion that class war transforms society.

material-over-identity.rationale: The doctrine ranks the nation and its spiritual identity above class and material interest, and rejects Marxian materialism.

military-superiority.rationale: The Doctrine (sections 3 and 13) holds that war brings out the highest human energies and that expansion, empire and power are signs of vitality.

minority-veto.rationale: Numbers and individual wills do not bind the state; the state binds individuals.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Doctrine (section 6) says neither monarchies nor republics are to be judged as eternal forms and notes monarchies that 'welcome the most venturesome social and political experiments', so a monarch is acceptable.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Doctrine says action should be motivated by holiness and heroism, not economics.

more-religion-public.rationale: The 1929 Lateran Treaty made Rome the centre of the Catholic world and placed religious instruction in public schools and Catholic marriage under Church rules.

nation-first.rationale: The Doctrine (sections 3 and 13) puts the nation-state and its expansion above international creations.

national-church-status.rationale: Under the Lateran Treaty Roman Catholicism was the state religion of Italy, ending only with the 1985 concordat.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Doctrine presents Fascism as the doctrine of a people 'rising again after many centuries of abandonment' against the decadence of liberalism (sections 8 and 13).

natural-rulers.rationale: The Doctrine (section 6) affirms 'the fertilising, beneficent and unassailable inequality of men' and a people realised in the will of the few or one.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Doctrine repudiates pacifism and holds that war brings out the highest human energy.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Doctrine (sections 10 and 12) says the Fascist State 'cannot be limited to a simple function of order and of safeguarding' and is no night-watchman.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Doctrine makes the State the creator of right and demands discipline and authority from every citizen.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Article 36 of the 1929 concordat required religious instruction in public primary and secondary schools.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The Doctrine (section 9) holds that a people is realised in the will of the few or even one, so selecting officeholders by chance is foreign to it.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Doctrine states that 'a party that totally rules a nation is a new chapter in history', and Mussolini endorses Rocco's call for an uncompromising attitude towards other parties.

organic-representation.rationale: Gentile and Rocco present the Corporations of Syndicates as the Fascist State's representative system, replacing the political individual of liberalism with the individual as producer.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Doctrine (section 11) criticises 'the preponderance of parliamentarism' and 'the irresponsibilities of assemblies' as problems Fascism solves.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Doctrine rejects democracy and rule by numbers.

party-controls-media.rationale: Gentile counts 'all the instruments of propaganda and education' among the Party's tools for making the Duce's will the masses' will.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Doctrine (section 10) says the State 'educates the citizens in civic virtues' and gives them a consciousness of their mission, and Gentile has it draw children into the Party.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The Doctrine stresses the essential value of labour and calls the Corporative System the place where workers' needs find expression within the nation.

person-over-state.rationale: The Doctrine places the state above the individual, whose liberty is a margin the state grants.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Doctrine (section 3) holds international creations extraneous to Fascism and (section 10) makes the nation-State the highest ethical form.

positive-liberty.rationale: Fascism rejects the materialist premise; liberty is duty within the state.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Doctrine (sections 6 and 10) makes the State the keeper and transmitter of the people's spirit 'in its language, customs and beliefs' and stresses tradition.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Doctrine makes the state absolute and the source of all value, so justice, policing and defence are state monopolies, never market services.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Doctrine (section 5) denies the Marxist conception of history and class warfare, and Rocco defends property and profit as socially useful.

property-fundamental.rationale: Rocco (1925) holds that private property is not a matter of justice but of social utility, so it is recognised only as far as it serves the community.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Rocco's Perugia address, endorsed by Mussolini, says socialism erred in making private property 'a matter of justice' when 'it is a problem of social utility', and the recognition of property is justified by that utility.

proportional-representation.rationale: In 1923 the Fascist government changed the electoral law so that the party group with the largest vote, even with only 25 percent, got an absolute majority of seats.

race-social-construct.rationale: The 1938 Manifesto of Race states that 'the concept of race is purely biological' and that human races exist as a material reality.

racial-pride.rationale: The Manifesto of Race calls the 'ancient purity of blood' the greatest title of nobility of the Italian nation and urges Italians to proclaim themselves racists.

recall-officials.rationale: The Doctrine (section 6) rejects governing by numbers through periodical consultations, and Rocco makes the State's authority absolute.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Doctrine (section 6) rejects governing by numbers through periodical consultations.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Under the 1926-34 system the State's National Council of Corporations, presided over by the head of government, could issue binding rules for economic relations between employers' and workers' associations, and each corporation was an organ of the State.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Doctrine (section 12) calls religion 'one of the most profound manifestations of the spirit', not a comfort for material suffering.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Doctrine says Fascism exacts discipline and an authority that dominates the interior of the spirit 'without opposition'.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Under Italian law of the corporative system, 'strikes and lockouts are regarded as penal offences' and labour disputes went to State labour courts.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Doctrine (sections 2 and 10) presents the nation-state as an ethical, spiritual whole that outlasts its members and gives their lives meaning.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The Doctrine subordinates the individual to the state and makes duty central.

self-ownership.rationale: The Doctrine subordinates the individual to the state and denies individual rights as primary.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Lateran Treaty and concordat gave the Church religious instruction in public schools, canon-law marriage, and an oath of loyalty from bishops.

separated-powers.rationale: Rocco (1925) says the authority of the State 'is absolute' and does not bargain or surrender any part of its field, and the Doctrine attacks 'the irresponsibilities of assemblies'.

single-common-good.rationale: The Doctrine (section 10) has the State 'harmonize' citizens' interests through justice and hold every group to a single national interest.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Doctrine makes the state the highest value, to be strengthened and not smashed.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Doctrine glorifies war and demands obedience.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Doctrine rejects materialism and calls fascism a spiritual and religious conception of life.

state-as-business.rationale: The Doctrine treats the state as an ethical and spiritual entity with a will of its own, not an enterprise serving customers who may leave.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the Marxist view of the state, holding it a higher ethical unity that stands above and shapes classes.

state-harmful.rationale: The Doctrine makes the state the foundation and source of all value and liberty.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Doctrine (section 12) says the Fascist State respects and protects religion and does not try 'to cancel the idea of God from the mind as Bolshevism tries to do'.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: The Doctrine (sections 12 and 13) makes the State an educator and promoter of the spiritual life that rebuilds 'the man, the character, the faith', not a neutral night-watchman.

strong-leader.rationale: The Doctrine (section 9) holds that a people is realised 'in the consciousness and will of the few or even of one only', and Gentile has the Party make 'the thought and will of the Duce' the will of the masses.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Britannica records that Mussolini's regime 'attacked political opponents' and 'dismantled free speech' once in power.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Britannica records that Mussolini's regime 'engaged in heavy surveillance' as part of its dictatorship.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state is the source of all value and its claims on citizens are legitimate.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Empire growth is an essential sign of vitality and decline its opposite.

total-state.rationale: The Doctrine (sections 7 and 10) calls Fascism 'a totalising concept' in which nothing human or spiritual exists outside the State.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Doctrine (section 10) has the State link 'through the centuries' those who built it, and traces the nation to Roman empire (section 13).

unions-run-economy.rationale: The Doctrine (section 8) opposes the unions of the labouring classes as bodies outside the State, which alone orders the economy through the corporations.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism puts the state above the individual as the source of all right, so law gets authority from the state, not from justice outside it.

vote-delegation.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the vote and rule by numbers.

war-builds-character.rationale: War alone raises human energy to its highest tension, according to the Doctrine.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Doctrine requires every individual to live within and for the state, so retreat from public life is condemned.

worker-ownership.rationale: Rocco rejects the socialist solution of collective organisation of production and keeps individual property rights in the Fascist doctrine.

workers-councils.rationale: Class-based rule is rejected; the state and corporations stand above classes.

workers-nation.rationale: The Doctrine denies class warfare as the agent of social change and unites producers in the Corporative System within the nation, with no class outside the State.

notes: Rules-7 pass. The earlier pass rested on Wikipedia pages; they are no longer evidence for any answer. Answers now rest on the full Doctrine of Fascism, Rocco's and Gentile's essays, Mussolini's speeches (1914-23), the 1926-34 labour statutes (ILO article), Britannica on the Lateran Treaty and the Italian regime, and the 1938 Manifesto of Race. Answers whose only support was a Wikipedia page were nulled unless a source now read settles them. Themes searched in the local corpora and on the web: economy and corporatism, property, strikes, parliament and elections, religion, race, women and family, empire and borders, education, press. Record sources for the regime after 1924 (economic policy such as the IRI and autarky, local government, population policy, colonial rule, women's rights, schooling) were looked for in Britannica pages that Britannica truncates behind a paywall, and the Fordham and Wikisource texts of the 1919 manifesto and 1927 Labour Charter could not be fetched, so those themes stay null.
